query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 1 at.% Al to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective alumina scale, resulting in a 30% reduction in oxidation rate at 800 °C in air, relative to the untreated material, without compromising its room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 800 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure-time: 5 h, Loading: No mechanical loading
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective alumina scale that prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy
generation.boundary: Temperature: 800 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure-time: 5 h, Loading: No mechanical loading
generation.uncertainty: The actual oxidation rate reduction may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions. The addition of Al may also affect the alloy's mechanical properties, which needs to be evaluated.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose both untreated and Al-added equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr samples to air at 800 °C for 5 h, and measure the oxidation rate using thermogravimetry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate of the Al-added sample is not reduced by at least 20% compared to the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified.
